# Case-study diagnostics

## Heat-kernel translation

Worst-translate total variation treats arbitrary group translates as if they
were physically admissible neighboring conditional states.  At small heat
time, separated translates are almost singular.  The useful local variable
exposes concentration but erases the good-field/collar condition required to
make the comparison physically relevant.  Diagnosis: a quantifier-domain
failure, not merely a weak constant.

## Frustrated conditioning

Conditioning a link on a center-frustrated boundary produces a conditional
law whose most likely configuration leaves one plaquette macroscopically
frustrated.  The microscopic conditional kernel has forgotten the action cost
stored in the boundary.  Diagnosis: boundary-state erasure.  Recovery requires
a charged contour or multi-link integration, not a stronger one-link bound.

## Moments versus adaptive domination

Bounds on fixed intersections do not determine the conditional probabilities
revealed after an adaptive history.  Diagnosis: loss of filtration/history
data.  The appropriate certificate is sequential and state-indexed.

## Action charge versus partition ratios

An energetic lower bound in a numerator becomes a probability bound only
after normalization.  Diagnosis: loss of entropy/free-energy information.
The recovery object is a uniform conditional partition-ratio theorem.

## Methodological payoff

These diagnoses select different repairs—restrict a quantifier domain, retain
a boundary state, enlarge the state by a filtration, or prove a normalized
ratio.  A single scalar “approximation error” cannot make these distinctions.
